title: Normalized affine Leray section equivalence before scalar extension
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes, and $F$ a quasi-coherent module on $X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Fix an injective resolution $I$ of $F$, a degree $p\in\mathbb N$, and an affine open $V\subset S$. Put $U=f^{-1}V$, $A=\Gamma(S,V)$, $h:U\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the restricted morphism followed by the canonical affine chart, $N=F|_U$ computed by open-immersion pullback, and $P=R^pf_*F$. Let $R$ be any augmentation-preserving restricted resolution data for $I$ on $U$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-open-choices]. Let $E_M:H^p_{\mathrm{Mod}}(U,M)\simeq H^p(U,M)$ be a family of additive equivalences natural for all module morphisms, with module right-derived sections [pqf-def-cohomology] and the Ext cohomology model [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison]. Define $e_H$ by applying $E$ to the restriction of $F$ and transporting through the canonical restriction/pullback isomorphism. There is an $A$-linear equivalence $e:HOver(h,N,p)\simeq_A\Gamma(P,V)$ whose value on $\xi$ equals the class map resolutionSectionClass for $R$, followed by the inverse resolution comparison for $f_*$, applied to $e_H^{-1}(\xi)$. There is no base-change scheme, ring extension, second resolution or flatness hypothesis.

proof.text: Transport the supplied natural comparison E through Mathlib restrictFunctorIsoPullback using H.mapLinearEquiv. This is the displayed additive eH. Naturality hE for multiplication by global functions shows compatibility with the A-action through h; the cohomology map of an isomorphism is linear.

Restrict f to f inverse V -> V. Ordinary higher images commute with open restriction and are quasi-coherent. Their positive cohomology on the affine scheme V vanishes. Apply the cocycle-normalized Leray degeneration theorem to obtain an invertible edge. Naturality for multiplication makes this edge linear over A=Gamma(S,V). Taking sections and using restrictAppIso identifies its target with Gamma(R^p f_*F,V).

The presheaf description identifies the edge with the map induced by the homology projection and sectionCohomologyTheta. The augmentation and components equations of R identify the restricted resolution section complex with the original complex evaluated on f inverse V. Augmentation-preserving resolution comparisons compute the same derived class map, giving precisely resolutionSectionClass followed by the inverse I.isoRightDerivedObj. Compose this bijective linear edge with eH inverse. This proves the normalization for every xi, including p=0, the empty open and the zero module.
